newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady on Wednesday in moderate trade with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. May wholesale inventories data, dealers said.
Wholesale inventories for May are forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.7 percent fall reported in April.

"Rates were quietly steady this morning except for some position adjustments in short dates. Some people are waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the U.S. May wholesale inventories figures," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations, as most people have squared their positions for the day," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday and Thursday/Friday were unchanged from Tuesday's common 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent, respectively. Week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, nine-months unchanged at 5-15/16 5-13/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
